title: Beneath Our Feet and O'er Our Head
description: Beneath Our Feet and O'er Our Head in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Reginald Heber wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 531 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Universal Warning of Death”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-neath our feet and o'er our head Is e-qual warn-ing given: Be-neath us lie the count-less dead, A-bove us is the heaven!

lines: Beneath our feet and o'er our head
Is equal warning given:
Beneath us lie the countless dead,
Above us is the heaven!
Their names are graven on the stone,
Their bones are in the clay;
And ere another day is done,
Ourselves may be as they.
Our eyes have seen the rosy light
Of youth's soft cheek decay,
And fate descend in sudden night
On manhood's middle day.
Our eyes have seen the steps of age
Halt feebly towards the tomb;
And yet shall earth our hearts engage,
And dreams of days to come?
Death rides on every passing breeze,
He lurks in every flower;
Each season has its own disease,
Its peril every hour.

licence: Public domain: Reginald Heber died in 1826.
credits: Words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
